input: Explore imposter syndrome workshops or webinars online

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: Knowing whether the user wants to passively watch recorded content, attend a live interactive workshop, or find a full course changes which platforms and resources to target entirely.

Imposter syndrome workshops vary hugely by audience — some are tailored for early-career professionals, others for women in leadership, academics, or specific industries — and the right fit depends on who the user is.
Whether this is for personal growth, a workplace initiative, or academic development affects the type of provider (coach, HR platform, university) and the framing of the content.
Budget is a major filter — free webinars, paid one-off workshops, and premium coaching programmes are very different options, and the plan must stay within what the user can spend.

Some people want evidence-based psychological frameworks (e.g. CBT-rooted), others want practical exercises, peer discussion, or motivational storytelling — the style shapes which workshops will actually resonate.
Time availability determines whether the user needs a short one-hour webinar, a half-day workshop, or something spread across multiple sessions they can fit around their schedule.
Understanding what outcome the user wants — reduced self-doubt, concrete coping tools, a certificate, or a community — determines what 'done well' looks like and which workshop delivers real value.

gold.taskTitle: Find and attend imposter syndrome workshops online
gold.taskDescription: The user wants to explore online workshops or webinars focused on imposter syndrome, but the specific intent, format, audience, and constraints are unclear.

questions.title: Are you looking for live sessions or recorded content?
questions.description: Determine whether the user wants a live, interactive workshop/webinar or is happy with pre-recorded on-demand content, as this filters the entire range of options.

questions.title: What is your professional background or career stage?
questions.description: Identify whether the user is a student, early-career professional, mid-level manager, senior leader, or in a specific industry, so the workshop audience can be matched appropriately.

questions.title: Is this for personal development or a workplace setting?
questions.description: Clarify whether the user is exploring this for themselves individually, for a team they manage, or as part of a company or academic programme.

questions.title: What is your budget for this — free, low-cost, or open?
questions.description: Establish a clear budget range to filter between free community webinars, paid single-session workshops, and premium coaching-led programmes.

questions.title: Do you prefer a research-based approach or practical exercises?
questions.description: Understand whether the user gravitates toward psychology-grounded frameworks, hands-on tools and activities, peer discussion, or inspirational speaker formats.

questions.title: How much time can you dedicate to this in total?
questions.description: Find out if the user needs something compact like a one-hour webinar, a half-day workshop, or a multi-week programme they can spread across their schedule.

questions.title: What does a successful outcome look like for you?
questions.description: Determine the user's desired end result — whether it is gaining specific coping strategies, building confidence, joining a supportive community, or earning a certificate — to match the right workshop.
